Europe is on track to expand its cored wire market from around USD 0.64 billion in 2025 to nearly USD 0.87 billion by 2031, registering a steady 6.10% CAGR and absolute growth of roughly USD 0.23 billion. Decarbonisation drives, including stricter CO₂ regulations and funding for green steel pilots, are nudging producers toward higher-purity alloying solutions, significantly lifting wire uptake.

Japan’s cored wire revenues are poised to edge up from roughly USD 0.17 billion in 2025 to USD 0.21 billion by 2031, translating into a 4.30% CAGR and USD 0.04 billion of incremental value. Automotive lightweighting programs and the nation’s concerted shift to hydrogen-based steelmaking are fostering demand for precise alloying feeds that minimise impurities.

Korea is forecast to grow its cored wire market from about USD 0.11 billion in 2025 to almost USD 0.20 billion by 2031, enjoying a 6.50% CAGR and roughly USD 0.08 billion absolute gain. Ambitious expansions in shipbuilding, offshore wind fabrication and high-strength steel grades encourage wire suppliers to innovate with tailored calcium and rare-earth formulations.

China’s cored wire segment will leap from approximately USD 0.42 billion in 2025 to near USD 0.73 billion in 2031, delivering an impressive 8.50% CAGR and about USD 0.31 billion in new revenue. Intensifying efforts to upgrade blast furnaces, elevate steel quality and phase out polluting induction routes drive aggressive adoption of alloy-laden wire feeding systems.

Within the broader North American bloc, the USA alone is set to advance from USD 0.14 billion in 2025 to roughly USD 0.17 billion by 2031, implying a 5.20% CAGR and nearly USD 0.03 billion additional sales. Federal infrastructure bills, re-shoring of manufacturing and rising oil-and-gas well interventions are sharpening focus on specialty cored wires for weld overlay and alloy control.
